name: Toothpaste on pimples
lead: Dabbing toothpaste on a pimple overnight is a long-circulating home remedy for acne. Practitioners say it dries out the spot.

Toothpaste is formulated for teeth: it typically contains abrasives, fluoride, surfactants such as sodium lauryl sulfate, flavourings and sometimes antibacterial agents [1]. Wikipedia's toothpaste article does not discuss use on acne, and its acne article does not list toothpaste among treatments [1][2].

paras: Typical toothpaste components include abrasives (8-20% of the product), fluorides, foaming surfactants, antibacterial agents and flavourants such as peppermint [1]. Sodium lauryl sulfate has been linked to oral tissue dryness and mouth ulcers in some people, and hypersensitivity reactions to polyethylene glycol-containing substances have been reported [1]. These observations concern the mouth and do not address facial skin.

card.summary: The classic overnight dab of toothpaste on a pimple; no studies were found and toothpaste is not designed for skin.
card.note: Ingredients such as surfactants and flavourings are reported to irritate oral tissue.

quick.overview:
Some people apply toothpaste to a pimple overnight, believing it dries the spot out.

No clinical studies were found, and standard references on toothpaste and acne do not describe this use.
quick.mechanism: Proponents point to drying ingredients such as abrasives and surfactants; no research confirms this effect on acne.
quick.risks: Sodium lauryl sulfate and other ingredients are reported to irritate oral tissues and cause sensitivity in some people.
